text:
Maria Chen: Quick heads-up — ran a cross-device autotune job this morning to validate seqlen-aware kernel choices for L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100. Putting findings here so we can pick presets.
Samir Patel: nice, initial numbers? :eyes:
Maria Chen: TL;DR: H100/A100 pick the new fused-attn kernel across seqlen ranges, L4/A10/T4 prefer legacy matmul kernels at long seqlens. We saw two surprising regressions on A10 at seqlen=512 after enabling continuous-batching tweaks.
Leo Wu: can you paste the perf table?
Maria Chen: pasted below (p50/p95 tokens-per-second and avg latency for a 1-token regen request pattern):
```
Device  | seqlen | kernel_chosen         | p50_latency(ms) | p95_latency(ms) | tokens/s
H100    | 128    | fused-attn-opt       | 7.8             | 13.4            | 950
A100    | 128    | fused-attn-opt       | 9.1             | 15.9            | 820
A10     | 128    | matmul-v3            | 12.3            | 28.4            | 410
L4      | 128    | matmul-smallbatch    | 18.2            | 45.6            | 220
A10     | 512    | matmul-v3            | 38.6            | 92.1            | 95   <-- regression after batching tweak
H100    | 512    | fused-attn-opt       | 22.0            | 40.2            | 340
```
Samir Patel: that A10 regression is worrying. Was the KV cache hit ratio consistent?
Maria Chen: good call. KV stats: cache hit ratio stayed ~96% across runs, but eviction churn spiked on A10 when sequence length crossed 384. Looks like KV workspace fragmentation + our allocator's slab rounding triggers extra memcpy.
Priya Nair: did you capture Nsight/NVTX traces?
Maria Chen: yes — attaching condensed trace excerpts (trimmed):
```
# A10 seqlen=512
[setup] allocate_kv_workspace: 3.2ms
kv_copy_back: 18.7ms
matmul_v3.exec: 12.1ms
batching_coalesce: 9.3ms
# H100 seqlen=512
allocate_kv_workspace: 1.0ms
kv_copy_back: 4.0ms
fused_attn.exec: 8.2ms
batching_coalesce: 2.1ms
```
Ben Thompson: so the big delta is kv_copy_back and allocator overhead on A10. Could be PCIe bandwidth + host memcpy. A10 in our infra is PCIe gen3.
Leo Wu: yep — H100 has NVLink and faster memcpy pathways in our setup. For A10 we should prefer kernel paths that minimize KV movement. Maybe pick a tail path that stays in-place and trades a bit of compute for less memcopy.
Samir Patel: does kernelselector allow a memcopy penalty heuristic? We have latency + copy_cost in the scoring but default weights favor flops.
Maria Chen: right now weights are tuned for H100-ish configs. We need architecture-aware weights per device family. I ran a quick experiment adjusting score = latency_est + 0.8*copy_est for A10 and it moved selection to a different kernel for seqlen 512 — latency improved 11% and p95 improved 18%.
Priya Nair: nice. Can we codify that into presets? e.g., presets/device_family: {A10, T4, L4} with copy_weight=0.8, fused_bias=-0.2?
Maria Chen: proposed YAML snippet for a preset:
```
# presets/autotune/a10_t4_l4.yaml
device_family: a10_t4_l4
score_weights:
  latency: 1.0
  copy_cost: 0.8
  kernel_stability: 0.2
fallback_threshold_ms: 60
inplace_preference: true
seqlen_buckets: [128, 256, 384, 512, 1024]
```
Samir Patel: fallback_threshold_ms=60 seems high for low-latency routes. What's the reason?
Maria Chen: it's for long seqlen streaming workloads where we prefer stable throughput vs an occasional 30ms spike. We can tune per SLA. Also added inplace_preference to bias towards kernels that avoid host<->device copies.
Ben Thompson: regressions after continuous-batching change — can we hotpatch the batching heuristic to be seqlen-gated? e.g., disallow batching_coalesce > X for devices without NVLink when seqlen>384.
Leo Wu: easy change: add device_property.has_fast_peer_copy flag and early-exit. I can push a quick guard: if (!has_fast_peer_copy && seqlen>384) limit_coalesce = min(limit_coalesce, 2).
Priya Nair: let's be careful with canary. infra-bot, can you queue a canary rollout to internal-dedicated-a10 pool with the guard?
infra-bot: Canary job scheduled: canary/2243 -> internal-dedicated-a10, rollout duration 30m, monitor p50/p95. Link: https://canary.redwood.test/2243
Samir Patel: thanks. Also suggest we add a KV hotspot profiler in autotune run so next iteration we can quantify memcpy vs compute tradeoffs automatically. Maria — can you add a flag --emit-kv-hotspots to autotune harness?
Maria Chen: on it. Plan: run full sweep across devices (L4,T4,A10,A100,H100) overnight with new scoring weights + kv hotspot capture. Will post results tomorrow morning.
Ben Thompson: also log the kernel selection decision path for each request (seed, seqlen, cache_hit, selected_kernel, score_breakdown) — helps debugging.
Maria Chen: will add.
Leo Wu: one more: for A10/T4 we should try a memory-layout tweak: pack KV in NCHW-ish contiguous pages to reduce memcpy ops. Might be low-risk.
Priya Nair: agree, add as a follow-up experiment.
Maria Chen: OK summary action items: 1) Infra canary with batching guard (Leo) 2) Maria: run full autotune with copy-weighted scoring + --emit-kv-hotspots 3) Ben: add request-level decision logs to debug console 4) Priya: experiment plan for KV packing layout.
Samir Patel: awesome. Ping me if canary looks bad and we'll roll back quick. :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: thanks team — will update thread with overnight results.
Maria Chen: (later) quick update — overnight sweep finished, attached condensed CSV with kernel selections per device and seqlen. Early highlight: copy_weight=0.8 fixed the A10 regression at seqlen=512; p95 improved from 92ms -> 74ms. H100 picks unchanged. Full CSV uploaded to /internal/tmp/autotune/2112345678-results.csv
Priya Nair: great, thanks. We'll use these as baseline for the next presets PR.
Maria Chen: filing a follow-up PR to presets repo after review. :rocket:
